chunks: Ali, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'From the signs of the Hour is the spread of paralysis and sudden death.'

key_terms.الْفَالِجُ: paralysis (often referring to stroke or widespread paralysis)

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the Hour mentioned in Shia hadith regarding health and death?
ai.summary: In Al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith linking widespread paralysis and sudden death to the signs of the Hour, reflecting the Shia scholarly tradition of interpreting physical and social decay as indicators of eschatological proximity. This narration underscores the interconnectedness of bodily afflictions and spiritual decline, serving as a reminder for believers to prepare for the unseen through increased devotion and moral vigilance.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘From the conditions of the Hour is the spread of paralysis and the sudden death’.
en.sarwar: 39. Ali has narrated from his father from af-Nawfafiy from af-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Holy prophet has said, ‘One of the signs of the coming of the Day of Judgment is the spread of paralysis and sudden death.’”
